newsitem.title: HUNGARY: GAZPROM HUNGARY BANK UNIT SEES EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: GAZPROM HUNGARY BANK UNIT SEES EXPANSION.

text.p: The central European banking arm of Russia's Gazprom have boosted its registered capital to 10 billion forints $54.04 million) from 1.1 billion forints since September 1996 and plans rapid business expansion, the daily Magyar Hirlap said on Wednesday.
Gazprombank, the financing arm of Russia's gas giant Gazprom, bought 100 percent of the subsidiary, Altalanos Ertekforgalmi Bank Rt (AEB), in August 1996.
The daily quoted AEB Chairman and CEO Mikhail Rakhimkulov as saying that Gazprombank planned to raise the subsidiary's registered capital further, to between 20 billion and 22 billion forints.
AEB boosted its balance sheet total in 1996 to 71 billion from 37 billion and sees a rise to above 125 billion forints by the end of this year.

The bank's 1997 pre-tax profit reached 1.3 billion forints in June, compared with an after-tax figure of 134 million forints in 1996, and is likely to rise to about three billion forint by the end of this year, Rakhimkulov said.

AEB finances Hungary's gas imports from Russia and plays an increasing role in Gazprom's borrowings, Magyar Hirlap said, adding that the bank planned to issue bonds worth $50 million to $75 million in cooperation with Credit Suisse First Boston later this year.
